summary: Sanders County, MT site first staffed 1929 from a tree; 50-ft L-4 tower later gone and cabin burned 1991; a 2020 proposal to move Priscilla Peak lookout there is unconfirmed.

facts.design: 1929 lookout tree and cabin; later a 50-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Tower and building removed or destroyed (sources differ on when); cabin burned in 1991; no source describes the site today

access.note: 2020 Forest Service proposal: access road NFSR 876 is open yearlong to public motorized use

events.note: Watch first kept from a tall tree near the summit; Fred Benson on the peak for the summer
Cabin built just down the ridge for the lookout
50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, per firelookout.com (the 2020 Ledger gives no date)
Sterling Clawson assigned to the lookout
Lightning-started fire reported by Clawson in July 1957; he went half a mile down the mountain to put it out
Last four miles of access road built
Road reported open to visitors in July 1958
Lookout station retired after its last season; the 2020 Ledger says the Forest Service later brought down the building and pole structure (no date given)
firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed; conflicts with the Ledger account of removal after 1969
Cabin at the foot of the tower burned in an accidental fire; the 2020 proposal blames an improperly installed wood stove
Forest Service proposed moving the Priscilla Peak lookout to Driveway Peak; completion not confirmed in sources read

corrections.why: firelookout.com names the Lolo National Forest, the 2020 Ledger quotes a Lolo National Forest archaeologist, and the 2020 proposal places the site in the Plains/Thompson Falls Ranger District. The Kootenai label appears only on the Forest Lookouts Montana page.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and the 2020 Ledger name the Lolo National Forest; the Forest Lookouts Montana page labels the site Kootenai National Forest. The story uses Lolo.

The 2020 Ledger says the Forest Service brought down the building and pole structure after the 1969 retirement; firelookout.com says the tower was destroyed in 1978; the 2020 proposal says all three structures on the site burned. The story reports all three accounts.
firelookout.com says 10 miles west of Thompson Falls; the 2020 proposal says approximately 11. The story gives a range.

sources.title: USFS proposes to move historic lookout

notes_for_editor: Brief listed agency as Kootenai NF; corrected to Lolo NF. Fate of the tower and building is contested (1969 removal vs 1978 destruction) and the story says so. The 2020 Priscilla Peak move is a proposal; no completion record found. The Forest Service project page for it (project 58117) showed no status in the copy read. Verify with Lolo NF before publishing any claim that the move happened. No photos gathered.
